drifted.spec_text: force_flush() ensures all mutations are durable on disk: it invokes a durable-flush trigger installed by the wiring layer via attach_flush_trigger and blocks until it returns, mapping trigger errors to StorageError (spec.md:163)
drifted.actual: force_flush maps trigger errors correctly (src/lib.rs:221-235), but the documented trigger FlushManager::trigger_flush always returns Ok(()) (src/flush.rs:177), because do_flush completes the served tickets whether or not flush_to_disk succeeded (src/flush.rs:246-257). A failed flush is therefore reported as durable. Spec line references (lib.rs:201-215/:111/:68) are stale; the current lines are :221-235/:131/:72.

drifted.spec_text: Recovery falls back to inactive region if active region is corrupt (spec.md:167); Recovery Algorithm: verify header CRC and entry CRCs; if active region corrupt, try inactive region (spec.md:299-300)
drifted.actual: Fallback happens only when the region header is corrupt or its flush_seq does not match (src/recovery.rs:53-66). A corrupt entry is skipped one sector at a time (src/on_disk.rs:341-344) and the region is accepted as a partial result, with no warning and no fallback. A multi-sector record misaligns the parse of every later record.

drifted.spec_text: Crash consistency: partial flush never corrupts previously-committed data (spec.md:193); 'Crash during step 2: old active region is still valid' (spec.md:291)
drifted.actual: After a fallback recovery, the superblock is returned unchanged (active_region still points at the corrupt region; src/recovery.rs:68-77). The next flush writes inactive_region_offset() (src/flush.rs:45-46), which is the only valid checkpoint. A crash before the superblock write (src/flush.rs:54) leaves both regions invalid, and recovery then formats the partition fresh (src/recovery.rs:79-84), losing all data and resetting flush_seq to 0.

drifted.spec_text: put(key, value) stores arbitrary binary data (0 to 128 KiB) by string key (spec.md:159)
drifted.actual: put does not limit key length (src/lib.rs:179). EntryRecord::serialize writes key_len as `len() as u16`, which truncates silently (src/on_disk.rs:233), but copies the full key (:242). Keys longer than 65535 bytes fail the CRC on recovery and are lost silently, along with entries after them.

drifted.spec_text: Multiple force_flush() calls coalesce into single flush operation (spec.md:170; US6 AC2 spec.md:140; plan.md:32)
drifted.actual: Coalescing is ticket-based: calls registered before a pass reads `requested` (src/flush.rs:213) share that pass; calls registered while a pass is in flight wait for the next pass (src/flush.rs:171-175). With nothing dirty, a call still waits for one worker wake-up, although no I/O happens (src/flush.rs:223-231). Doc comments src/flush.rs:79 and :153 are out of date.

drifted.spec_text: External persistence-wiring API (... snapshot_entries, mark_flushed ...) (spec.md:175); plan.md:101 'mark_flushed(new_seq) [reset dirty_count]'
drifted.actual: snapshot_entries records the dirty count it covers (src/lib.rs:103-104); mark_flushed subtracts exactly that count and clears it (src/lib.rs:113-121). Without a snapshot before it, mark_flushed leaves the dirty count unchanged. An interleaved second snapshot_entries overwrites the single recorded slot (src/lib.rs:53), so only one flusher may drive the pair at a time.
